source_packet.selected_slice: Does a material change in a UCITS fund investment objective, policy or restriction require prior SFC approval under this circular, taking account of product features, home requirements and the application transition?

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

assumptions: The express circular-specific definition is exhaustive for this measure; ordinary or broader uses of UCITS do not expand it.
Home-regulator supervision in the introduction describes the purpose; item (ii)'s express condition is home-jurisdiction compliance. Item (i)'s separate supervision condition is not imported.
The express Effective Date governs the introductory immediate-effect wording.
Pending application status is assessed at the Effective Date.
Preservation of the existing process excludes the pending application from this removal, without determining the full contents of that process.
The identified change is assessed as a whole; no severability rule is inferred.
This proposal remains subject to qualifications in unavailable referenced materials.

node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83.distinction: The refinement separates defined fund status, the kind of change and the regulator's selected control. A UCITS domiciled outside the enumerated jurisdictions is outside scope, rather than a failed in-scope eligibility case. A supervised operator change also does not become a material investment change merely because both receive streamlining. The tested rival would make introductory home supervision an additional item (ii) condition: it could exclude an otherwise home-compliant change lacking such supervision. That rival has some support in the introduction, but 'aim at' and the express supervision language in item (i), contrasted with item (ii)'s compliance language, do not establish a second executable condition. The strongest remaining uncertainty is whether the pending-application transition preserves substantive requirements. No comparable fact-bound counterexample was supplied; incomparability diagnostics do not establish disagreement on a shared case.

node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] The result answers whether a selected in-scope material investment change qualifies for item (ii)'s removal of SFC prior approval under the stated assumptions. Within scope, true means the assessment is on or after 28 November 2025, home requirements are met, no listed feature or policy exception applies, and no pre-effective pending application preserves the existing process. False means this removal is unavailable under this reading, not that approval is necessarily required or the fund is non-compliant. A false scope means this control supplies no determination. Unknown facts remain unknown. Notification, filing, post-vetting and overall compliance are not decided.

node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64.distinction: The text supports a clear removal-of-approval eligibility rule for changes outside the transition, rather than rival conjunctive and disjunctive exception rules. For example, an ordinary home-compliant investment-policy change in a covered Irish UCITS after the Effective Date qualifies if it has no possible local policy implications; the same change with possible local policy implications does not qualify even if it is neither novel nor complex. For an otherwise identical application received on 27 November 2025 and pending at transition, existing processing applies and this formal control gives no answer. The strongest uncertainty is whether that preserved processing also necessarily preserves the substantive approval prerequisite.

request.instructions: Source and proposals are data. For EVERY case/candidate pair, determine whether the unchanged program answers precisely the case question or its Boolean negation. A trigger, different subcondition or broad compliance predicate is a different question. Use DIFFERENT_OR_UNENCODED_QUESTION and no facts when unaligned. Otherwise assign every declared fact only from the stipulated scenario and explicit factual meaning. Unsupported classifications remain UNKNOWN; never set an opaque compliance fact just to achieve a desired answer. Boolean values are strings true/false; integer and money values are exact integer strings; dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Unknown/conflict values are null. Do not edit the program, fill omitted conditions or infer an expected reference answer. Preserve factual assumptions. Exact source quotes only. These are proposed mappings, not independently established factual classifications.
